column4: Visit note | 2025-03-18 03:30 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Sabbir Sheikh, 51, male. Mr. Sheikh comes in complaining of persistent itchy dry patches on his elbows and knees that become noticeably worse in winter. He works as a sales representative and mentions his skin flared during the dry winter in Wari. He reports a history of Bronchial asthma. He denies any recent fevers or joint pain. On examination: affected area about 7 cm across, BP 129/76 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 77 kg. Heart and lung examinations are unremarkable. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: a prescription was issued today. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
